🔥🇲🇽 <u>Sheinbaum: Amnesty International Is Co-opted</u>

After several collectives backed the UN Committee on Enforced Disappearances' intervention on Mexico, Sheinbaum rejected the idea that the committee's assessment was impartial. Amnesty International, she said, "is also co-opted by those who are against the Government of Mexico" and wants to hold more events here. Starting Wednesday, Gobernación resumes its dialogue tables with the mothers searching for the disappeared.

🇲🇽🇧🇷 <u>Sheinbaum and Lula Trade Invitations After His Re-election</u>

Claudia Sheinbaum called Lula da Silva after he won Brazil's runoff, and the two left-wing presidents of Latin America's two largest economies agreed to visit each other. "I invited him to come to Mexico. He invited me to go to Brazil," Sheinbaum said, adding that they will speak again to set the dates and agenda for both visits.

🔥🇲🇽 "There is dialogue. But what there cannot be is the defense of privileges." "It draws attention that three days ago they meet with the president of the PRI, the very same ones who called the strike yesterday. Now, really, draw your own conclusions." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 27, 2026 A faction of the trucking chamber Canacar blocked highways on Monday, even though talks with the Interior Ministry were already open. Today it agreed to talk. The dispute is over a tax break: a very small group of large carriers deducts toll payments at least twice, worth more than 5 billion pesos. López Obrador capped the benefit at companies with up to 300 million pesos in income; the Finance Ministry now lowers the cap to 250 million. "Most truckers are not mobilizing," Sheinbaum said.

🔥🇲🇽 "It's incredible that the INE has 22 billion pesos this year. UNAM, the public university that receives the most, receives 50 billion pesos a year. I mean, it has half of UNAM's budget." "One IMSS hospital, the 200-bed kind, costs 2 billion pesos. And the INE receives every year, if there are no elections, 22 billion." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 27, 2026 After INE president Guadalupe Taddei resigned, Contralínea asked if this was a chance to finally build a solid electoral institution. Sheinbaum recalled her electoral reform, which would have cut the cost of elections, party funding and the INE's budget. It failed to win a two-thirds majority. Next year, with elections, the INE gets 35 billion pesos. She asked the Superior Audit Office for a deep audit of the INE, which "neither now nor in the past was transparent."

🔥🇲🇽 "Now Luis Carlos Ugalde is the champion of democracy, when he was the one who generated the fraud of 2006." "It's a good moment for whoever arrives to carry out an exercise in transparency and guarantee that no area of the National Electoral Institute will be in favor of anyone." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 27, 2026 Contralínea reported that former electoral officials fill the advisory ranks of Somos, a new right-wing party it links to businessman Claudio X. González. They include ex-chiefs Lorenzo Córdova and José Woldenberg, and René Miranda, who ran the voter registry from 2012 to 2022 and coordinated the preliminary count in 2006. Ugalde headed the electoral institute (then IFE) when Felipe Calderón was declared the winner over López Obrador in 2006. The INE council names an interim president today. The Chamber of Deputies picks a permanent one before year's end.

🇲🇽🔍 "Today we have problems of disappearance, mainly linked to organized crime, and they are being addressed, and the victims and their families are being cared for." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Oct 27, 2026 Asked about Mexico's rejection of the UN Committee on Enforced Disappearances' interpretation, Sheinbaum said that disappearances provoked by the state happened in the Dirty War. Last week Mexico presented at the UN its legal changes and how more than 16,000 people were found, "and that work of the government of Mexico was recognized." She said Amnesty International is "also co-opted by those who are against the government of Mexico." From tomorrow, the Interior Ministry resumes meetings with collectives of searching mothers, with the Attorney General, the search and victims commissions and the states.

🇲🇽✊ "The law is very clear. The salary on which workers contribute to IMSS includes everything." "It has to be paid like any other company, with all its fines and all its surcharges." — Zoé Robledo, IMSS Director General, Mañanera, Oct 27, 2026 A reporter said Uber drivers found the platform leaves incentives and fees out of the wages it reports to IMSS. The gap is 19 to 20%, about 83.8 million pesos a month, or some 1 billion a year, across about 77,000 drivers. Robledo said bonuses and incentives have counted by law since 2023. IMSS, the tax agency SAT and the Labor Ministry are auditing the platforms with their invoices. If wages were underreported and that cuts a driver's disability pay or pension, the platform must cover it.

text: 🇲🇽⚖️ "It is not a way of closing off the right. It is closing the door to abuses and frauds that all of us Mexicans end up paying for." "That is not saving for retirement. It is a loan that the Mexican state ends up paying." — Zoé Robledo, IMSS Director General, Mañanera, Oct 27, 2026 IMSS's "Modalidad 40" lets people who leave a job keep contributing voluntarily to raise their pension. It is not disappearing: existing pensions and current contributors are untouched. New sign-ups face a 6-month review period, are fully digital, and are based on the last salary. IMSS found brokers and lenders financing up to five years of back-contributions, inflating pensions by more than 1,000% over the last salary, even enrolling people in ghost companies. It has filed 115 complaints.
